what_happened: Direct verification confirmed git-commit-scoped.sh's existing V9 gate already classifies an out-of-repository pathspec distinctly (its own ledger, exit code, and WARN text), but git-commit-phase.sh's upstream Containment Self-Check drops the same path earlier with the generic undeclared-scope message before V9 ever sees it -- a reusable precedent for the fix rather than new logic.

Confirmed cause 1 (external source store) is deployment-relative: in this repository, .claude-extensions.json's core.source_dir resolves inside this repo's own git root (not external), so this repository's own agent-system/** containment drops (tasks 444, 450) are caused by cause 2 and the addendum's regenerated-surface gap, not by a genuinely external repository. The externality was reproduced instead against BimodalLogic's own .claude-extensions.json, which points the identical absolute path outside its own repo root.

Premise re-validation: the description's claim that this repository's core source_dir resolves to 'a different git repository' is false IN THIS REPOSITORY -- jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json yields /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core and git rev-parse --show-toplevel from inside it yields /home/benjamin/.config/nvim, this repo's own root; agent-system/ exists and is tracked here. The claim holds only for a deploy-consumer repository. Plan design retargeted at the general consumer case with an explicit inertness guarantee for this repository.

validate-artifact.sh's Tier Justification check caught three genuine discrepancies in the first draft (two phases claimed suite coverage where suite_selection_select returns __FULL_SWEEP__ because their paths are new and unmapped; one phase under-named a suite). Also surfaced that the DEPLOYED .claude/scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh resolves one more suite than the source-store copy, because the selector enumerates test files present on disk and the deployed tests/ tree carries extension suites the core source store does not -- the validator's own output is therefore the authoritative union for a justification line.

Phase 2's Tier Justification one-hop dependent run (run-all.sh --only test-backfill-file-scope.sh,test-gate-out-derived-staleness.sh,test-gate-out-repair-reporting.sh,test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh,test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh,test-skill-base-lifecycle.sh,test-validate-artifact.sh) surfaced 25 pre-existing failures in test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh and test-gate-out-repair-reporting.sh (status persistence cases: implementing vs completed/partial), neither related to file_scope harvesting, plan-file-scope-harvest.sh, or validate-artifact.sh, and neither touched by this phase. The two suites this phase actually edited (test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh, test-validate-artifact.sh) pass in full. Likely the subject of a concurrently dispatched sibling task's own test-failure sweep.

Phase 5's own stated verification criterion (verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4 exits 0) cannot be satisfied at Phase 5's own close: gate 3 (check-extension-docs.sh) correctly reports the 4 new scripts created in Phases 1 and 4 (source-store-path-lib.sh, commit-source-store-path.sh, and their two test suites) as undeclared in manifest.json's provides.scripts array, plus one doc/skill cross-reference gap -- both are explicitly Phase 6's own declared work (manifest derivation via sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write), not Phase 5's. check-record-versioning.sh and check-task-references.sh (gate 4, and the record-versioning check) both report 0 BLOCKING findings on all three files Phase 5 edited. Resolved immediately by proceeding to Phase 6, which re-runs the complete gate set (including gates 3/4) after the manifest sync and deploy, per Phase 6's own verification criteria -- no residual work is left behind beyond the very next phase in this same plan.

verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow (run post-deploy during Phase 6) reported 2 failures, neither caused by this task's edits: (1) gate 10 (validate-state.sh --deep) timed out at its 60s ceiling; re-run directly it took 53-58s and genuinely FAILED once on a stale TODO.md date-stamp line (regenerated content differed only in the 'Updated <date>' line after the calendar date advanced since the last regeneration) then PASSED cleanly on immediate re-run after specs/TODO.md was regenerated via generate-todo.sh -- a date-rollover timing artifact, not a content defect from this task. (2) gate 24 (lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh) reported 2 pre-existing dead /ide references in agent-system/extensions/memory/context/project/memory/{memory-setup,memory-troubleshooting}.md, wholly outside this task's declared scope and untouched by any phase of this task.

Gate 8 (run-all.sh) inside verify-deploy.sh's complete-gate-set run could not complete cleanly: specs/.gate-lock was held throughout by a live, legitimate concurrent process (confirmed via ps: pid 1121698/1121700/1124447, 'run-all.sh --only test-askuserquestion-rehome.sh,test-deploy-propagation.sh,test-routing-resolution.sh,test-update-task-status.sh,test-lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh,test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh' -- exactly task 555's own declared-scope suite set), i.e. the concurrently-dispatched sibling task's own verification run, not a stale lock. This task's own test suites were therefore run directly, bypassing the shared gate-lock entirely, and all pass: test-git-commit-phase.sh 84/84, test-commit-source-store-path.sh 20/20, test-source-store-path-lib.sh 21/21, test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh 48/48, test-validate-artifact.sh 136/136. Separately, the complete gate set's remaining two findings (gate 10's validate-state.sh --deep 60s-ceiling timeout, confirmed to PASS cleanly at 73-74s wall time outside that ceiling; gate 24's lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh flagging 2 pre-existing /ide references in agent-system/extensions/memory/context/project/memory/{memory-setup,memory-troubleshooting}.md) are both confirmed unrelated to this task's declared file_scope. Per this dispatch's Batch Gate Deferral directive, the authoritative full-batch gate run is deferred to the once-per-invocation batch-level stage.
